---
title: "DVC (Data Version Control)"
---

We use [DVC](https://dvc.org/) to version-control large data files (models, input datasets) without storing them in Git.
DVC tracks file hashes in `.dvc` files committed to Git, while the actual data lives on remote storage.

## Authentication

DVC uses the standard AWS credentials from the root `.env` file:

```ini
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID='<MinIO access key>'
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='<MinIO secret key>'
```

Pixi activation scripts use python-dotenv to load `.env` before running any task. The MinIO endpoint and region are non-secret and are committed in `.dvc/config`, so new contributors do not need to create `.dvc/config.local` for authentication. Run DVC through Pixi so the credentials are available:

```sh
pixi run dvc <command>
```

::: {.callout-note}
Existing clones may still have remote credentials in `.dvc/config.local`. Remove those credential fields after migrating `.env` from `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY` and `MINIO_SECRET_KEY` to `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
:::

## Pull data

Prefer pulling only the data needed for the stage you are working on. To fetch a stage and its dependencies without reproducing it, use [`dvc pull`](https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/pull):

```sh
pixi run dvc pull rwzi --with-deps
```

Only pull all tracked data when you have enough disk space (currently ~100GB), time, and just want all data local:

```sh
pixi run dvc pull
```

If you have local changes that you want to overwrite, add `--force`.

## Remotes

The MinIO remote is configured in `.dvc/config`:

| Remote | URL | Purpose |
|:-------|:----|:--------|
| `minio` (default) | `s3://ribasim-nl/dvc` | Primary DVC cache on MinIO |

## Pipeline

The DVC pipeline is defined in [`dvc.yaml`](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/blob/main/dvc.yaml). Dependencies determine the order in which stages run:

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-dvc-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "DVC pipeline DAG (click to zoom)"
%%| file: _dvc-dag.mmd
```

```{=html}
<style>
#fig-dvc-pipeline { cursor: zoom-in; }
#fig-dvc-pipeline.fullscreen {
  position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 9999;
  background: white; cursor: zoom-out;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  padding: 2rem;
}
#fig-dvc-pipeline.fullscreen svg { max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%; }
</style>
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const fig = document.getElementById("fig-dvc-pipeline");
  if (fig) fig.addEventListener("click", () => fig.classList.toggle("fullscreen"));
});
</script>
```

## Reproduce stages

During development, reproduce only the stage you are working on. The `--pull` option asks DVC to fetch missing dependencies before running the stage with [`dvc repro`](https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/repro):

```sh
pixi run dvc repro --pull rwzi
```

Without `--pull`, `dvc repro` only uses data already present in the workspace or local DVC cache. Other useful options are [`--force`](https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/repro#-f) to run a stage even when DVC considers it unchanged and [`--single-item`](https://doc.dvc.org/command-reference/repro#-s) to run only the named stage without reproducing its upstream dependencies.

::: {.callout-warning}
A full `pixi run dvc repro` currently takes several days. We only run full reproductions in parallel on the SLURM cluster using `repro.sh`; see [Running on SLURM](slurm.qmd).
:::

## Pushing changes

After producing new outputs (running pipeline stages or adding new data), push to the remote:

```sh
pixi run dvc push
```

Do this before pushing the updated `dvc.lock` file to Git, so the data hashes referenced therein are available to everyone.

Most MinIO access keys handed out are read-only.
Reach out if you need help uploading data.
In general we update all results after a full cluster run.
